An AST scan will extract the compact source navigation facts.

The first command will scan and print the facts. The second command will write the files. This keeps the artifact text separate from the observation gate.

A single self-contained script is cleaner than two separate commands. It would compute line numbers directly and print only filenames and sizes to stdout. The risk is mis-copying line numbers.

The second script will re-parse the AST to generate the files. This avoids hand-copying line numbers. The first command will be a compact AST survey to confirm module shapes. The risk is that a large survey output could exhaust the two-call budget.

The generator will be self-contained. The survey will only validate module existence. The generator will extract entrypoints, observer and publisher functions, SHA-256 hashes, and argparse entry points from the AST.
